A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AlignMMBench and CritiqueVLM. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated or renamed in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluator-versus-human agreement experiments in Table 2 and evaluations of ten VLMs in Table 3.

after.justification: v3 retains the evaluator experiments and reports an expanded VLM leaderboard, alignment-score analyses, and a no-image control.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same ChatGLM3-6B evaluator, reference-answer-based scoring, general and task-specific prompts, fine-tuning procedure, and GLM-4 question rewriting. The expanded construction descriptions do not establish a changed underlying method. The new alignment score is an evaluation metric.

E1.justification: The Chinese benchmark retains its thirteen tasks, single-turn and multi-turn coverage, and 4,978 question-answer pairs. v3 adds a GPT-4o evaluation without images in Table 3, introducing a limited test scenario with different available inputs.

E2.justification: Table 3 expands from ten to sixteen VLMs, adding Qwen2-VL, Claude, InternVL2, ShareGPT4V, LLaVA-v1.5, and InstructBLIP. The original models remain, including renamed entries identifiable through Table 4. The evaluator comparison retains ChatGLM3-6B, ChatGPT, and GPT-4.

E3.justification: Section 5.3.2 introduces alignment score, the inverse average standard deviation of scores across paraphrases, alongside average performance. Table 3 adds an image-removal control. The category analysis also changes its selected subset from models averaging above 5.0 to above 6.0. The evaluator split and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 extends v1's illustrative paraphrase example into a quantitative robustness analysis across models. It adds the no-image ablation, backbone/language/size comparisons, question and answer length distributions, and a CritiqueVLM-versus-GPT-4 meme-scoring case study. The earlier Mona Lisa scoring example is removed; the reasoning example is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for leaderboard performance. The new standard-deviation-based alignment score measures variation across paraphrased questions rather than uncertainty across repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises many retained-model scores: GPT-4o's reported average changes from 6.57 to 6.41 and CogVLM2's from 5.86 to 5.81. New Qwen2-VL and Claude entries both report 6.51. v3 also adds alignment values, the no-image GPT-4o average of 2.13, and supplementary findings. Table 2 remains numerically unchanged. The PDFs do not explain all leaderboard score revisions.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a formal definition of alignment score, defining paraphrase groups, within-group score means and standard deviations, and their inverse-average aggregation. v1 contains no corresponding mathematical definition. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction add a distinct claimed contribution: quantitatively assessing alignment through robustness to semantically equivalent prompts. Combined performance and alignment scores now support a four-class model characterization. This substantially extends v1's benchmark-and-evaluator claims, which otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets performance and consistency combinations as different strengths or weaknesses in alignment versus visual/language components. Section 5.3.4 adds training-language and model-size interpretations, while acknowledging that differing corpora prevent isolating architectural effects. The Chinese-only scope and dependence on reference answers remain stated limitations.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 and Appendix A.5 newly document collection keywords, over 20,000 crawled images, hash-based filtering, annotation checks, approximately ten annotators, and roughly sixty entries per annotator per day. v3 also supplies model sizes/backbones, states zero-shot evaluator testing, and replaces the project-site link with a repository link. Conversely, v1's datasheet, including dataset licensing, distribution, and maintenance details, is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds judge-related references and discussion, including MLLM-Bench, GPT-4V as an evaluator, and Prometheus/Prometheus 2, plus newer model references and citations supporting Chinese-context motivation. The principal positioning against existing multimodal benchmarks remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The introduction and construction narrative are substantially revised. Detailed task definitions move from Section 3.1 to Appendix A.1, the standalone leaderboard becomes Section 5.3 within Experiments, and the appendices are reorganized around definitions, analyses, examples, and implementation details while dropping the datasheet.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v3 adds the performance-versus-alignment plot, length histograms, backbone table, and evaluator-comparison illustration; Table 3 gains Size and Align. columns and additional rows. Existing figures are resized or relocated, the category chart gains percentages, and the two-panel scoring illustration loses its Mona Lisa panel.

improvement.justification: The no-image control strengthens evidence of visual dependence, and the expanded collection and annotation documentation makes benchmark construction more auditable. Broader model comparisons also improve the evaluation's usefulness. These gains are limited by removal of the datasheet and unresolved inconsistencies: Section 5.3.1 still identifies GPT-4o and CogVLM2 as leaders although Table 3 places Qwen2-VL and Claude above them. The new alignment metric's component-level interpretations also lack independent validation, supporting a limited overall improvement.
